title.narrative: Second West Bengal Development Finance Program

description.narrative: The proposed program seeks to facilitate the continuation of a comprehensive fiscal consolidation program in West Bengal initiated in 2012. This will generate fiscal savings and, thereby, assist West Bengal to augment growth-enhancing development financing and improve delivery of public services.

description.narrative: Investment in the state particularly in social and economic sectors, improved and sustained

Gross capital formation (as a percentage of GSDP) in the state improved by 2 percentage points by FY2019 (2015 baseline: 35.4%). Progress/Status: Gross capital formation (as a percentage of GSDP) in the state improved by 11.6% points to 47.0%c Data Source: Annual finance accounts and annual economic review of GOWB Actual value:

100% premium paid for at least 95% of the registered beneficiaries under Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (National Health Insurance Scheme) (2015 Baseline: premium paid for 81% of registered beneficiaries). Progress/Status: Achieved. Swasthya Sathi replaced the RSBY in FY2017 and covers 100% of premium payments of beneficiaries since its inception. Data Source: Annual finance accounts and annual economic review of GOWB Actual value:

Drop-out rate in classes 3-10 reduced by 0.75% (2016 Baseline: Classes 3-4: 2.23%; classes 5-7: 3.46%; and classes 8-10: 14.08%). Progress/Status: Data awaited Data Source: Annual finance accounts and annual economic review of GOWB Base year: 2016 Baseline value: N

OPD introduced in all 34 new BRGF hospitals (2016 Baseline: None). Progress/Status: Achieved. 41 hospitals have been built with OPD facility. Data Source: Annual finance accounts and annual economic review of GOWB Base year: 2016 Baseline value: N
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Expenditure rationalization efforts accelerated Indicator: At least 70% VRS/ERS is disbursed to targeted employees of the four state transport corporations and Shalimar Works Limited (2016 Baseline: Not disbursed). Progress/Status: Partially complied with. 1,368 employees have been considered for VRS under the program out of which 733 are in tranche 2. However, since 80% of VRS payments in the last two rounds have been made till now, the effective achievement in tranche 2 is 689 against the tranche 2 target of 1483, a shortfall of 794 employees.
891 VRS-eligible employees did not opt for the scheme and retired in regular course. Cumulatively, the total retirement is 2,253, which is higher than 70% of the targeted 3,025 employees (2,118 employees). Data Source: Annual Report of the Finance Department, and annual budget statements of GOWB Actual value:

Output: Expenditure rationalization efforts accelerated Indicator: At least 90% of total financial liabilities of Neo Pipes and Tubes Company Limited and National Iron and Steel Company Limited (Rs.462.13 Crore) have been completely settled (2016 Baseline: Not settled). Progress/Status: Achieved. Liabilities of NPT and NISCO totaling ₹478.63 crores settled (more than the mandated 90%) Data Source: Annual Report of the Finance Department, and annual budget statements of GOWB Actual value:
